+# duckdbcli - SQL command line client for DuckDB
+
+A small `sqlite3`-like console client, using the mORMot parameters parser
+(`Executable.Command`), for the three DuckDB flavors of the framework:
+
+| mode | option | notes |
+|------|--------|-------|
+| embedded engine | `-d file` or `file` (default `:memory:`) | needs `duckdb.dll` / `libduckdb.so` (64-bit) |
+| mormot.db.proxy | `-p host:port --root name -u user -w pwd` | any database published by a `TSqlDBServerSockets` |
+| Quack | `-q quack:host[:port] -w token` | native client, no library needed; token may be set by `DUCKDB_TOKEN` |
+
+```
+duckdbcli my.duckdb -c "select count(*) from t"
+duckdbcli -q quack:localhost -w secret
+duckdbcli -p 127.0.0.1:8899 --root duck -u user -w pass -m json -c "select * from t"
+duckdbcli -f script.sql -m csv --noheader
+```
+
+Interactive statements end with `;`. Dot commands: `.tables`, `.schema [table]`,
+`.mode table|csv|json|line`, `.timer on|off`, `.version`, `.help`, `.quit`.
+Run `duckdbcli -h` for all options.
+
+Build with FPC or Delphi: `fpc -Mdelphi duckdbcli.dpr` (with the mORMot `src`
+sub-folders in the unit path).
+
+## Benchmark against the official `duckdb` CLI
+
+Scripts are in the [`bench`](bench/README.md) folder. Dataset: the public
+[`train_services.parquet`](https://blobs.duckdb.org/train_services.parquet)
+(380,959 rows, 8 columns), queried through a view-only catalog database as
+described in <https://duckdb.org/2026/10/07/view-only-mode>.
+
+### Execution environment
+
+- Cloud VM, Linux 6.18 x86_64, 4 vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.80 GHz, 15 GB RAM
+- Official `duckdb` CLI v1.5.6 and the same `libduckdb.so` v1.5.6 for `duckdbcli`
+- `duckdbcli` built with FPC 3.2.2 (`-O3`), Quack client using protocol version 1
+  (the one of the released DuckDB 1.5 `quack` extension)
+- Everything on localhost: Quack and `mormot.db.proxy` servers on the same VM,
+  Parquet file read from the local disk (no network involved)

+  which loads the `httpfs` and `quack` extensions on first use

+
+| Query | official embedded | duckdbcli embedded | official Quack | duckdbcli Quack | duckdbcli proxy |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| `count(*)` | 22 | 50 | 137 | **7** | 7 |
+| top 10 stations (group by) | 28 | 56 | 138 | **11** | 12 |
+| group by type, min/max | 33 | 63 | 142 | **17** | 20 |
+| filter on `train_number` | 32 | 67 | 146 | **18** | 18 |
+| `select *` (380,959 rows) | 809 | 847 | 1265 | **901** | 4764 |
+

+# CLAUDE.md - mORMot 2
+
+Guidance for every Claude Code session in this repository. Folder-specific notes live in
+`src/*/CLAUDE.md` (e.g. `src/db/CLAUDE.md` for the database layer and the DuckDB TODOs).
+
+## Code quality: mORMot intent, not only mORMot style
+
+From Arnaud Bouchez's review of the AI-written DuckDB PR #666
+(https://github.com/synopse/mORMot2/issues/423#issuecomment-6218806358, 2026-10-16):
+the code was correct and well tested and *looked* like mORMot, but on closer look it was
+"correct but sloppy". Upstream expects performance-minded, non-redundant code. Rules:
+
+- **Parse once, reuse.** Never query/parse the same metadata repeatedly (e.g. a column's
+  logical type). Compute it once at prepare/first-step time and cache it.
+- **No duplicated code paths.** Factor shared logic into one function instead of
+  near-identical copies per call site or per type.
+- **Reuse existing framework code** instead of re-implementing it. Before writing any
+  converter, search the core units: date/time via `mormot.core.datetime.pas`
+  (`TSynSystemTime`, ISO-8601 helpers), GUID/UUID via the existing `TGuid` functions,
+  number/text via `mormot.core.base` / `mormot.core.text` / `mormot.core.unicode`.
+- **Avoid transient `RawUtf8`** (and other temporary managed strings) in hot paths such as
+  per-row / per-column loops: write directly to a `TJsonWriter`/`TTextWriter`, use a stack
+  buffer (`ShortString`, `TTemp*`), or pass `PUtf8Char` + length. Favor explicit
+  `PUtf8Char` when talking to C APIs.
+- **Specialized fast conversions** for hot types (e.g. 128-bit HugeInt to text with an
+  internal scale parameter) instead of generic, slow arithmetic.
+- **No `packed record`** for C API struct mirrors unless the C side is packed: it is much
+  slower on arm32/aarch64 and can break alignment.
+- **Benchmark against the naive path** before keeping an "optimization" or a convenience
+  feature. Example: DuckDB `BindArray` still executed one statement per row and was slower
+  than plain inserts - pure bloat. Prefer the mechanisms the ORM already uses
+  (e.g. `TSqlDBConnectionProperties.OnBatchInsert`).
+- **Keep the footprint small.** Do not add API surface, options or helper classes that the
+  framework does not need; less code that reuses the core beats more "complete" code.
+- **Tests:** no exception should be logged during a normal test run; skip tests cleanly when
+  an optional library is missing (and on unsupported bitness).
+
+## mORMot defaults (details: `docs/mORMot2-SAD-Recommended-Patterns.md`, Part A.1/A.2)
+
+- Use the framework types on every path it serializes: `RawUtf8` (not `string`),
+  `RawByteString` (not `TBytes`), `TDynArray`/`TDynArrayHashed` over `array of T`,
+  `TRawUtf8List` (not `TStringList`), `TDocVariant`/`IDocDict` for schema-less JSON.
+  `string` only at the UI/RTL boundary.
+- Build text/JSON/SQL with `TTextWriter`/`TJsonWriter` or `FormatUtf8`, never by repeated
+  concatenation or `Format`.
+- Respect the unit layering in `src/FOLDER-DEPENDENCIES.md` (core -> lib/crypt -> net -> db ->
+  orm/rest/soa -> app/ui/...). Conditional defines come only from `src/mormot.defines.inc`.
+- Diagnostics via `TSynLog`, never `WriteLn`. No swallowed exceptions / bare `except`.
+- Match the neighbouring code: `///` documentation comments on public API, existing
+  naming, existing helper functions. Read recent upstream commits on the same unit to see
+  how Arnaud refactors - that is the target style.
+

+### VARIANT columns (DuckDB 1.5+)
+
+VARIANT results are currently returned as JSON text, **without decoding the binary
+layout**: `DuckDBVariantSql()` re-executes the statement wrapped in
+`SELECT #1 AS "a", NULLIF(#2::JSON, 'null'::JSON) AS "b" FROM (sql)` so that DuckDB
+does the conversion (embedded: `TSqlDBDuckDBStatement.ExecuteVariantAsJson`, Quack:

+  converter, search the core units: date/time via `mormot.core.datetime.pas`
+  (`TSynSystemTime`, ISO-8601 helpers), GUID/UUID via the existing `TGuid` functions,
+  number/text via `mormot.core.base` / `mormot.core.text` / `mormot.core.unicode`.

+  per-row / per-column loops: write directly to a `TJsonWriter`/`TTextWriter`, use a stack
+  buffer (`ShortString`, `TTemp*`), or pass `PUtf8Char` + length. Favor explicit
+  `PUtf8Char` when talking to C APIs.

+  internal scale parameter) instead of generic, slow arithmetic.
+- **No `packed record`** for C API struct mirrors unless the C side is packed: it is much
+  slower on arm32/aarch64 and can break alignment.

+  than plain inserts - pure bloat. Prefer the mechanisms the ORM already uses
+  (e.g. `TSqlDBConnectionProperties.OnBatchInsert`).

A small sqlite3-like console client for the embedded DuckDB engine, any
mormot.db.proxy server, and a remote DuckDB Quack server (native client, with
no DuckDB library), with a benchmark against the official duckdb CLI in
ex/ThirdPartyDemos/tobfel/duckdb-cli.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,78 @@
+# duckdbcli - SQL command line client for DuckDB
+
+A small `sqlite3`-like console client, using the mORMot parameters parser
+(`Executable.Command`), for the three DuckDB flavors of the framework:
+
+| mode | option | notes |
+|------|--------|-------|
+| embedded engine | `-d file` or `file` (default `:memory:`) | needs `duckdb.dll` / `libduckdb.so` (64-bit) |
+| mormot.db.proxy | `-p host:port --root name -u user -w pwd` | any database published by a `TSqlDBServerSockets` |
+| Quack | `-q quack:host[:port] -w token` | native client, no library needed; token may be set by `DUCKDB_TOKEN` |
+
+```
+duckdbcli my.duckdb -c "select count(*) from t"
+duckdbcli -q quack:localhost -w secret
+duckdbcli -p 127.0.0.1:8899 --root duck -u user -w pass -m json -c "select * from t"
+duckdbcli -f script.sql -m csv --noheader
+```
+
+Interactive statements end with `;`. Dot commands: `.tables`, `.schema [table]`,
+`.mode table|csv|json|line`, `.timer on|off`, `.version`, `.help`, `.quit`.
+Run `duckdbcli -h` for all options.
+
+Build with FPC or Delphi: `fpc -Mdelphi duckdbcli.dpr` (with the mORMot `src`
+sub-folders in the unit path).
+
+## Benchmark against the official `duckdb` CLI
+
+Scripts are in the [`bench`](bench/README.md) folder. Dataset: the public
+[`train_services.parquet`](https://blobs.duckdb.org/train_services.parquet)
+(380,959 rows, 8 columns), queried through a view-only catalog database as
+described in <https://duckdb.org/2026/10/07/view-only-mode>.
+
+### Execution environment
+
+- Cloud VM, Linux 6.18 x86_64, 4 vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.80 GHz, 15 GB RAM
+- Official `duckdb` CLI v1.5.6 and the same `libduckdb.so` v1.5.6 for `duckdbcli`
+- `duckdbcli` built with FPC 3.2.2 (`-O3`), Quack client using protocol version 1
+  (the one of the released DuckDB 1.5 `quack` extension)
+- Everything on localhost: Quack and `mormot.db.proxy` servers on the same VM,
+  Parquet file read from the local disk (no network involved)
+- CSV output redirected to `/dev/null`; median of 9 runs (5 for the multi-statement

@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+# CLAUDE.md - mORMot 2
+
+Guidance for every Claude Code session in this repository. Folder-specific notes live in
+`src/*/CLAUDE.md` (e.g. `src/db/CLAUDE.md` for the database layer and the DuckDB TODOs).
+
+## Code quality: mORMot intent, not only mORMot style
+
+From Arnaud Bouchez's review of the AI-written DuckDB PR #666
+(https://github.com/synopse/mORMot2/issues/423#issuecomment-6218806358, 2026-10-16):
+the code was correct and well tested and *looked* like mORMot, but on closer look it was
+"correct but sloppy". Upstream expects performance-minded, non-redundant code. Rules:
+
+- **Parse once, reuse.** Never query/parse the same metadata repeatedly (e.g. a column's
+  logical type). Compute it once at prepare/first-step time and cache it.
+- **No duplicated code paths.** Factor shared logic into one function instead of
+  near-identical copies per call site or per type.
+- **Reuse existing framework code** instead of re-implementing it. Before writing any
+  converter, search the core units: date/time via `mormot.core.datetime.pas`
+  (`TSynSystemTime`, ISO-8601 helpers), GUID/UUID via the existing `TGuid` functions,
+  number/text via `mormot.core.base` / `mormot.core.text` / `mormot.core.unicode`.
+- **Avoid transient `RawUtf8`** (and other temporary managed strings) in hot paths such as
+  per-row / per-column loops: write directly to a `TJsonWriter`/`TTextWriter`, use a stack
+  buffer (`ShortString`, `TTemp*`), or pass `PUtf8Char` + length. Favor explicit
+  `PUtf8Char` when talking to C APIs.
+- **Specialized fast conversions** for hot types (e.g. 128-bit HugeInt to text with an
+  internal scale parameter) instead of generic, slow arithmetic.
+- **No `packed record`** for C API struct mirrors unless the C side is packed: it is much
+  slower on arm32/aarch64 and can break alignment.
+- **Benchmark against the naive path** before keeping an "optimization" or a convenience
+  feature. Example: DuckDB `BindArray` still executed one statement per row and was slower

+## DuckDB Provider: Review Notes and Future Optimizations

+Source: Arnaud Bouchez review of PR #666 (`mormot.db.raw.duckdb` / `mormot.db.sql.duckdb`),

+**What DuckDB is for in mORMot:** an analytical (OLAP) query engine over large datasets
+(CSV, Parquet, attached PostgreSQL...), not a replacement for SQLite3 as in-process
+transactional/memory database. Row-by-row INSERT speed is far below SQLite3 - do not
+benchmark or sell it on insertion numbers.
